newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourses gear up for co-operation talks.
newsitem.headline: German bourses gear up for co-operation talks.

text.p: Leading representatives of Germany's eight regional securities exchanges are to meet late next week in Frankfurt to discuss possible nationwide co-operation, bourse officials said on Friday.

The move followed a meeting of the Frankfurt, Berlin, Duesseldorf and Munich exchanges, which already have a co-operation agreement and are keen for the smaller bourses in Stuttgart, Bremen, Hanover and Hamburg to join, they said.

Wolfgang Peterhoff, managing director of the Duesseldorf bourse, told Reuters he had been invited to discuss co-operation proposals hammered out at the meeting on Wednesday but said he had agreed not to give further details.

In the past, Germany's small exchanges have held back from linking up with other bourses for fear of being overwhelmed and obscured by larger rivals, particularly by the Frankfurt stock exchange, which dwarfs all the rest.
Two years ago the German regional bourses agreed a comprehensive cooperation proposal for the first time, but differences of opinion meant the proposal was never approved.

However Hans-Joachim Feuerbach, managing director of the Stuttgart bourse, said the smaller bourses had made a proposal in August for a co-operation agreement and were expecting a response to that next week.

Earlier this week, the Boersen-Zeitung newspaper said Deutsche Boerse AG, the Frankfurt-based umbrella group for all the exchanges, was planning to centralise all German stock exchange data in one site.
Deutsche Boerse declined comment on next week's talks on Friday.
